win_rate_controls.note: Always-home backs the home side every game. Always-favourite backs whichever side the market makes favourite, so the two coincide only on games where home is favoured. Both are measured, not asserted.

correlations.definition: realised final margin against realised final total, same game — the dependence that makes multiplying a side and a total invalid
our side error against our total error, same game
correlations.source: computed from model_outputs.csv (side and total rows, same game)
correlations.context: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The received wisdom that margin and total move together is not supported by this data: the correlation is close to zero and its 95% interval contains zero. That means a side x total combination in the same game is close to a product of independent events here. The invalid-multiplication rule in this project therefore rests on same-team and same-player dependence, not on a margin/total link. A correlation printed without its n and its interval would have hidden this.

correlation_policy: Correlations are computed only from numbers present in the price store or from official final scores. Any pair with n < 200 is suppressed rather than printed. n is published with every value.

bets_needed_to_show_profit.q: how many bets before a bettor at this true rate is distinguishable from BREAK-EVEN, not from a coin

luck_panel.explanation: At -110 a bettor must win 52.38% to break even. Distinguishing a 55% bettor from a coin at 5% significance and 80% power takes thousands of bets, which is precisely why raw win rate and season ROI are forbidden as ranking rules here. These counts assume independent bets; parlays raise the required count because outcomes cluster.

game_parlays.note: requires a validated joint probability; marginal multiplication is invalid under the measured dependence

same_game_parlays.note: blocked by the margin/total dependence reported in correlations
